record.context_brief: Coset-law identities for skew lattice varieties
record.original_question: Determine whether coset law-like identities can always be described so as to determine a variety of skew lattices, or whether some varieties of skew lattices do not permit characterization by such coset law-like identities.

evidence.quote: Can we always describe coset law-like identities that can determine a variety of skew lattices?
Or are there varieties of skew lattices that do not permit such characterization?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra (S; ∨, ∧) with two associative idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities x ∧ (x ∨ y) = x = x ∨ (x ∧ y) and (x ∧ y) ∨ y = y = (y ∨ x) ∧ y. Green's relation D on a skew lattice is a congruence whose quotient S/D is the maximal lattice image, and each D-class is a maximal rectangular band. Given comparable D-classes A > B in S, the D-class B partitions A into cosets, giving rise to coset bijections between rectangular bands. A "coset law-like identity" is an equation (or quasi-identity) built from terms of the form C ∨ x ∨ C, C ∧ x ∧ C (with C ranging over D-class representatives) that captures relationships among coset decompositions arising from distinct pairs of comparable or incomparable D-classes (such as the chain law: for D-classes A > B > C, C ∨ a ∨ C = C ∨ a' ∨ C iff B ∨ a ∨ B = B ∨ a' ∨ B and C ∨ b ∨ C = C ∨ b' ∨ C whenever a > b, a' > b'; and the analogous diamond law). 

Question: Is it the case that every variety of skew lattices can be axiomatized (within the variety of all skew lattices) by some collection of coset law-like identities of this form? Equivalently, does there exist a variety of skew lattices that admits no characterization by any set of coset law-like identities?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the collection of open problems from NCS 2018. Available sources on coset structures in skew lattices (Pita Costa, Cvetko-Vah, and related work) describe specific coset laws (chain law, diamond law) and varieties such as categorical and distributive skew lattices, but no source found resolves whether every variety of skew lattices can be characterized by coset law-like identities.

status_evidence.title: On the coset structure of a skew lattice
status_evidence.snippet: Studies coset decompositions and coset laws in skew lattices.
status_evidence.claim: Coset laws are an active topic but the general axiomatization question is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Open problems from NCS 2018
status_evidence.snippet: Can we always describe coset law-like identities that can determine a variety of skew lattices?

status_evidence.title: On the coset structure of distributive skew lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Describes specific coset laws (chain, diamond) for distributive skew lattices.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific instances of coset laws are known; general question remains.
